summary:
Jujuy is a province of Argentina and stands under the national framework. No Jujuy-specific statute, provincial court ruling, provincial protection measure or documented enforcement incident was identified in the source inventory.

The only Jujuy-specific signal in the sources is an April 2025 report datelined Buenos Aires, in which trans activists said police violence against trans and travesti sex workers has worsened and is worst outside the capital, naming Jujuy among the more conservative interior provinces where the situation is "even more so". That is activist characterisation of the province rather than a documented Jujuy incident, and no named Jujuy organisation, victim or case accompanies it.

Jujuy has no local hate-crime reporting infrastructure that produces province-level records, so no Jujuy-specific count of anti-trans violence exists. The province sits under the national observatory's aggregate picture, which is not disaggregated by province or by victim group.
tangentialFactors:
The characterisation of Jujuy as a more conservative interior province is the only geographic differentiation the sources offer; it is not supported by any Jujuy-specific incident, date or case.

No Jujuy-based trans organisation, provincial human rights body or provincial court appears in the inventory, and no provincial measure adding to or subtracting from the national framework was found.

Because no provincial records are produced, an assessment of conditions in Jujuy rests on national-level data and on activist accounts of interior provinces generally, rather than on evidence gathered in the province.
localsOnly:
Trans residents of Jujuy depend on the national framework for identity documents and health care; no provincial provision altering that position was identified.

The police-violence account concerns residents working in sex work, a group the source names specifically as trans and travesti sex workers, and describes conditions in interior provinces as worse than in the capital.

No provincial body monitors or publishes hate-crime data for Jujuy, so residents have no local record of anti-trans violence and their experience appears only within the national aggregate.
outOfScopeNotes:
No Jujuy-specific statute, provincial court ruling or documented enforcement incident was identified; the province's position is drawn from the national framework and from activist statements about interior provinces.

The claim that Jujuy is among the provinces where police violence is worst rests on unnamed activists interviewed in Buenos Aires. No Jujuy incident, date, victim or police unit is named.

No provincial hate-crime figures exist, so whether anti-trans violence in Jujuy runs above or below the national pattern is not sourced.
